photos.c: Above: Stephen Sharp (stage 6), Phil Wicks (2), Jonathan Blackledge (5), Spencer Barden (4), Alaster Stewart (1) and Tim Watson (3) receive the Ian Logan Trophy – Belgrave’s fourth year of being top of the pile at Rushmoor Arena.  Only Stephen and Jonathan remained in the squad from 2004’s winning line-up.
“Sweatshop” Surrey CC League Race 1 at Brockwell Park, and Phil Wicks (9) and Stephen Sharp (1) slug it out at the front of the field.
With “Sweatshop” Surrey Cross Country League race less than one minute old, Phil Wicks has made clear his intentions.  He went on to claim his first league win.  Photo by Steve Wicks.
Phil Wicks laid his cards on the table at Lloyd Park, pushing on hard from the start, but it was Thames Hare & Hounds’ John McFarlane (263) who held all the aces.

Above: The start of the Eastleigh 10k on March 19th.  The race included the CAU Inter-Counties Championship and Belgravians were racing in some unfamiliar vests.  In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind  these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).  To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent).  Maclean's winning time was 29:47, Mays was second in 30:00 and Phil Wicks 3rd in 30:02.  Belgrave won the team race and Surrey the Inter-County Championship. Full result and report in the previous issue.  Photo by Steve Wicks.

Above: Start of the South of Thames Championship in Brockwell Park: Dave Anderson, Pete Willis (20), Mike Trees (18), James McMullen (Epsom Oddballs 142), Will Clark (Epsom & Ewell 137), Alan Barnes (Herne Hill 175), James Connor (Kent AC), Phil Wicks (19), Dean Lacy (Cambridge H 51), Alex Bodin.

Above: A mile gone in the men’s race and Barry Royden (847 Medway & Maidstone) holds a narrow lead with Matt Ashton (3 Aldershot F&D), Darren Deed (61 Bedford &C) and Phil Wicks (100 Belgrave) in echelon. Just behind Royden is Huw Lobb (Bedford), Dominic Bannister (Shaftesbury) and Andy Robinson (Newham & Essex Beagles).

Happy with a seventh successive year in the medals at the National Road Relay. Standing (left to right) Gerry North, Gordon Biscoe, Bill Laws, Brian Pritchard, Tom Osment, Maureen Pritchard, Zara Chidoub, Mark Pollard, Jonathan Blackledge, Janet Blackledge, Mike Blackledge, Neil Speaight, Alan Mead, Padraic Buckley, Paul Freary, Eric Hall, Pete Willis, Hazel Mead. Front row. Mavis Hall, Charles Jones, Richard Ward, Simon Jones, Malachi Byansi, Will Cockerell, Pat Mead, Phil Wicks.
Gold medals came wholesale for Phil Wicks – First in the ERRA & UKA individual championships and a member of the winning team in both championships as well.

NATIONAL 6-STAGE ROAD RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
Yes, we’ve brought you pictures like this before – but while our lads are able to notch up such great victories, we’ll have no hesitation in bringing you further such images. Left to right: James Kelly (stage 2), Phil Wicks (6), Stephen Sharp (1), Mark Miles (5), Jonathan Blackledge (3) and Simon Jones (4)

NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
A third National title of the Autumn season came Belgrave’s way at the end of a riveting race at Berry Hill Park, Mansfield. It was only the second time in our history that we’ve managed to pull this one off. Left to right: Mark Pollard (stage 2), Stephen Sharp (1), Phil Wicks (4), Mark Miles (3).
Above: Phil Wicks’ 14:46 on the final leg was on a par with Gary Staines run in 1996 and the efforts by Dave Anderson and Spencer Barden in our record breaking run of 2003.

Phil Wicks makes a fast start in the 2008 English National Cross Country Championship at Alton Towers. He placed second, only the third Belgravian in our history to do so (the others being Vic Blowfield in 1948 and Allen Graffin in 2002. Birhan Dagne has won the women’s race and Kassa Tadesse the junior men’s race – but we patiently wait for a senior men’s winner! Photo by Alan Mead.
They’ve done it again! National 6-Stage Road Relay Champions for a seventh time. Left to right above: Stephen Sharp (Captain), Nick Goolab, Steve Davies, Simon Jones, Phil Wicks, Neil Speaight.

Right: A set of medals was a possibility for the seniors but things didn’t go our way and only Phil Wicks (6197) ran up to expectations. Others pictured left to right are Mal Byansi, Russell Dessaix-Chin, Knut Hegvold, and to the right of and behind Phil – Pete Willis, Will Cockerell, James Kelly and Lander Eguia. Photos by Alan Mead.
